subject: Dedicated capacity: deal-driven fleet sculpting & prompt sampling
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lark.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan.price@lark.ai, procurement@lark.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial traffic sample + ask — dedicated capacity for Lark product

Jonas / Redwood team,

Thanks — attaching a condensed token sample (lark_token_sample.csv) and a short product brief. We're exploring a Dedicated plan for our customer-facing assistant and need a quick sizing sketch to run internally. High-level asks:
- Recommended GPU mix to support our traffic profile (concurrency + burst).
- Expected tokens/sec and cost ballpark (per-1M tokens).
- Guidance on quantization/8-bit tradeoffs vs accuracy for long-form outputs.
- KV cache recommendations for session affinity and multi-turn chat.
- Canary / rollout playbook: how to seed and fallback.

Quick product notes:
- Region: US-west primarily, single-region for now with DR to us-east.
- Traffic: broad estimate today ~1.2M requests/day; want to plan for 3x growth in 12 months.
- Mix: chat-style Q&A (~70%), long-form generation & summarization (~30%).
- SLOs: short-chat p95 below 350ms; long-form can be higher (p95 < 2.5s) but p99 considered for fallbacks.

Can you confirm an initial capacity sketch and assumptions by EOD Oct 5? Also would like a short mutual-action-plan (MAP) for pre-sales steps + procurement redlines.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform
LarkAI

Attachments: lark_token_sample.csv (csv)
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lark.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic sample + ask — dedicated capacity for Lark product

Alex — thanks for the sample and the brief. Looping Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (pre-sales sizing) so we can assemble a short sketch. A few clarifying q's that will materially change recommended fleet: 

1) Session behavior: when you say 1.2M requests/day, is that API calls or end-user sessions? Do sessions maintain a long KV history (many turns) or are they mostly stateless per request?
2) Burst profile: do you have any dayparting or marketing-led peak days (e.g., Black Friday style surges) — what's the 5-min and 1-hour peak multiple vs baseline in the samples?
3) Long-form distribution: you said 30% long-form — is that 30% of requests but these generate 70% of tokens? Any p95/p99 token sizes for long-form? Even a small tail (>2k tokens) changes memory footprint needs.
4) Quantization tolerance: are you okay with a small (human-evaluated) hit to output fluency to save 2–3x on memory and throughput? If not, we keep more A100-class memory in the plan.

Initial assumptions we're likely to model (we can adjust):
- avg prompt: ~200 tokens, avg response (mixed) ~420 tokens, token/service-call ~620 tokens total.
- concurrency target to plan for initial deployment: 900 sustained concurrent in us-west with 3x burst to 2700 for 10-minute windows.
- baseline growth: 3x over 12 months as you noted; sizing will include headroom for that.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync Monday Oct 4 to walk the sample and validate tails. After sync we'll produce a 1-page fleet sketch (GPU SKU mix, rough tokens/sec, expected p95 cost).

I will draft the MAP including procurement steps and required telemetry (token tracing, per-route latency) to unblock pricing.

- Jonas
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

> On Thu, Oct 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM Alex Chen <alex.chen@lark.ai> wrote:
> > attaching lark_token_sample.csv
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lark.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@lark.ai>, procurement@lark.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic sample + ask — dedicated capacity for Lark product

Thanks Jonas — answers inline:
1) API calls fairly close to user sessions; we keep a 10-turn window on average (~KV of last 10 exchanges). Some customers use longer context; estimated that ~8% of sessions keep >15 turns.
2) Peak pattern: baseline is steady weekdays; marketing events cause ~6x 1-hour peaks and short 15-minute spikes up to ~10x.
3) Long-form: for the long-generation cohort (30% of reqs) average response ~950 tokens; p95 ~1.8k; p99 ~3.2k (small number of ultra-long transcripts).
4) Quantization: product team prefers fidelity for long-form outputs; open to testing 8-bit for short-chat only.

Region: single primary region us-west, failover us-east. Canary plan: 5% seed, scale to 25% over 48–72 hours before full cutover.

I've attached a slightly expanded token sample (same CSV) — please include a rough cost per 1M tokens and a GPU SKU breakout in the sketch. Also confirm whether you can support a DR failover routing policy that spins up an additional reserved pool in us-east (we'd want defined RTO).

Appreciate it — can you share the MAP + sketch by EOD Monday Oct 5?

Alex

Attachments: lark_token_sample.csv (csv)
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lark.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: deal-driven fleet sculpting & prompt sampling

Alex — thanks for the clarifications and the sample. Attached is a short capacity sketch (Lark_Dedicated_Sketch_v1.pdf) plus a recommended MAP and assumptions table. Highlights below — this is a pre-sales sketch, not a final commitment: 

Summary assumptions (we used conservative tail estimates):
- Traffic baseline: 1.2M requests/day; modeled 3x growth over 12 months.
- Token mix: avg prompt 200 tokens; avg response (mix) 620 tokens; long-form cohort avg 950 tokens, p99 ~3.2k as you reported.
- Session behavior: per-session KV window ~10 turns; tail sessions >15 turns ~8%.
- Peak/burst: 10-minute burst ratio up to 6x; 15-minute microburst up to 10x.

Preliminary fleet recommendation (initial pilot):
- GPU mix: 6x H100 (high throughput) + 3x A100 80GB (memory-heavy long-form work) in us-west reserved pool.
  - H100 nodes handle short-chat traffic & high concurrency paths with quantized short-chat models.
  - A100 nodes host the long-form models and sessions requiring large KV caches.
- Autoscaling cushion: capacity headroom to absorb 3x baseline over 30-minute scaling window; microburst mitigation via dynamic enqueueing and short-lived overflow to a small hosted pool for graceful degradation.
- Estimated sustained tokens/sec at baseline (mixed): ~18k tokens/sec across the reserved pool; peak burst headroom target ~54k tokens/sec.
- Canary: start at 5% traffic (as requested), 48–72 hour ramp to 25%, monitor per-route token traces and quality regression.

Quantization guidance:
- Short-chat: safe to run 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants — substantial throughput gains.
- Long-form: recommend FP16 / 16-bit or mixed precision on A100 to preserve quality; pilot 8-bit on a subset and validate with your eval prompts.

Operational asks from Lark to finalize sizing:
- Annotated prompt/response examples for the top 10 routes (we used sampling but need route-level token distributions).
- Confirmation of acceptable fallback behavior (e.g., degrade to hosted small-model for 99.9th percentile overrides).
- Legal/procurement contact for SOC2 evidence & draft SOW procurement redlines.

Attached: Lark_Dedicated_Sketch_v1.pdf (pdf) — contains per-SKU throughput estimates, rough cost per 1M tokens under different quantization strategies, and a one-page MAP for procurement + integration steps.

Next steps:
- If this looks reasonable, we'll schedule an internal tech deep-dive with Karthik to convert this sketch to a firm capacity plan and show expected latency curves by route.
- Marissa to own the MAP; Jonas to run the tech validation.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Pre-Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
